newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra picks A$47 mln Tracor target drones.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra picks A$47 mln Tracor target drones.

text.p: Australian Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said on Wednesday Tracor Inc would supply unmanned aircraft to tow targets for the Australian Defence Force.

McLachlan said the new system, known as the Kalkara, was based on a high performance, recoverable jet powered drone aircraft that tows aerial targets, and would replace the elderly Australian Jindivik drones in 1998.

The A$47 million contract with Tracor Inc would include 20 target aircraft, two ground control stations and ground support equipment covering nine years of target system operation, he said in a statement.

"Kalkara will be used by the Royal Australian Navy and Royal Australian Air Force for exercising and evaluating surface-to-air-missiles, and air-to-air-missiles, as well as ship-borne anti-air and anti-missile defence systems," he said.
The system would be operated and supported by Australian industry, mainly through ASTA Defence, which is part of the Australian subsidiary of the Boeing Co, he said.
